title: Canonical nomenclature: what each word denotes, and which spec defines it

provenance.note: the specs these terms point at
CK versus GECK has been conflated more than once

prose: The retrieval vocabulary answers 'what words match'. This file answers 'what does the word DENOTE', which is a different question and the one that causes real errors. CK and GECK are the canonical example: they have been conflated repeatedly, GECK is a Fallout 3 and New Vegas editor, and it is not the tool in use. type is what a program should switch on. spec points at the machine-readable definition, so a term is never a label without a definition behind it. This file is the join between the human-readable corpus, the machine-readable specs and the retrieval index.

entries.name: CK
entries.note: Fallout 4 Creation Kit. The authoring host. Builds match the game at 1.11.240.

entries.name: GECK
entries.note: A Fallout 3 and New Vegas editor. NOT the FO4 CK and NOT in use. A separate peer tool on the replacement list, to be modernized through our own mod later. Conflating this with CK has caused repeated wasted work.

entries.name: xEdit
entries.note: FO4Edit 4.1.5f x64, build 7C57FA01. Community record editor and headless script host. Replaces the CK for record validation and generation where possible.

entries.name: Creation Engine
entries.note: The runtime. Hosts the Papyrus VM and the wire.

entries.name: Papyrus
entries.note: The scripting language. Compiler version 2.8.0.4 in use.

entries.name: Layer A
entries.note: The BSScript vtable slot that lets native code intercept a Papyrus call. DOES NOT EXIST YET. This is the central blocker.

entries.name: Layer B
entries.note: The Papyrus-visible API. Compiles and deploys. Calls into Layer A, which is absent.

entries.name: wire
entries.note: Native-to-Papyrus data path. The protocol doc is partly fiction; see HANDOVER section 11 before trusting it.

entries.name: control plane
entries.note: Where a human or another provider's model sits in to run tasks. This is the mod's reason for existing as a product, and it was MISSING from the retrieval objectives until the alignment audit.

entries.name: S0
entries.note: Prove a compiled .psc reaches a native we registered, with no F4SE. UNPROVEN.

entries.name: Tier 1 / Tier 2 / Tier 3
entries.note: Address resolution strategies, in preference order. The surface reports which tier resolved each probe so triage can explain itself. 18/18 resolve via Tier 1.

entries.name: F4SE
provenance: verified: no loader in the game root
entries.note: NOT a dependency, NOT a target API, NOT deployed. Studied for structural logic and scope. SKSE is its Skyrim counterpart, so SKSE-gated capability is a candidate for PIP-MON to supply rather than a prohibition.

entries.name: CommonLibF4
entries.note: Reverse-engineered engine layouts, vendored, 350 files. Unlike F4SE this is a LAYOUT library: depending on it is depending on facts about the game. Holds BSScript.h and VTABLE_IDs.h, the most direct lead to Layer A.

entries.name: ESL
entries.note: A flag in the record header, 0x00000200. Not a separate container.

entries.name: Creation Sync
entries.note: Authoring in the CK, playing in the game, one mod, validated by both.

entries.name: SKIP
entries.note: The check could not run. NEVER reported as PASS. 'We did not look' and 'we looked and it is fine' are different facts.

entries.name: L-IN
entries.note: Runs inside Fallout4.exe or CreationKit.exe: the Papyrus VM, Layer A and B, anything holding a game address. Shares the frame budget and the CPU with the renderer. Cost ceiling: zero-alloc in the hot path, never block a frame. A log line here costs real milliseconds of the player's frame.

entries.name: L-HOST
entries.note: A separate module inside one of the two host processes. Inherits the host's crash domain, so a crash in L-HOST is indistinguishable from a crash in Bethesda's code to whoever is sitting in front of it.

entries.name: L-BE
entries.note: overseer_cli, the Rust vlink-protocol crate, ai_watcher, the retrieval tools, the dashboards. Shares nothing, and can be stopped and restarted without touching the game. Cost ceiling effectively none, which is exactly why the expensive work belongs here.

entries.name: placement axis
entries.note: WHERE code runs and what it may cost. ORTHOGONAL to the T0-T5 data-flow axis. A thing can sit at any tier in any layer. Conflating the two axes is why four Papyrus scripts ended up doing backend work in the one place they could least afford to do it.

entries.name: ring buffer
entries.note: The in-engine telemetry budget is a fixed preallocated ring, not a stream. The engine writes compact fixed-size records; the backend drains over the wire at whatever rate it likes; when the backend is slow the oldest records are overwritten. This is what makes the backend free to be verbose SAFELY: asking for more detail cannot make the engine do more work, because the writing was already paid for and already bounded.
